introduction: On this Sunday, Moses rejoices when two men outside the camp receive the Spirit and prophesy: if only all the Lord's people were prophets. In the Gospel, Jesus tells his disciples not to stop someone who does good in his name, and warns them never to cause a little one to stumble. Saint James condemns the rich who cheat their workers. Let us welcome the Spirit wherever he works.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord's law is perfect and gives life. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may recognize and welcome the work of the Holy Spirit wherever it is found. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians of other churches and communities: that we may grow together in unity and common witness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For workers who are cheated of their wages or exploited: that justice may be done and their cries heard. Let us pray to the Lord.
For children and vulnerable people: that they may be protected from all harm and never caused to stumble. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may cut out of our lives whatever leads us into sin. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you pour out your Spirit on whom you choose. Free us from jealousy, make us generous to all who do good, and keep us from every sin. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Whoever is not against us
reflection.body:
In the first reading, God shares the spirit that is on Moses with seventy elders. Two men, Eldad and Medad, are not at the tent with the others, but the Spirit comes on them too, and they prophesy in the camp. Joshua is upset and wants Moses to stop them. Moses answers with great generosity: "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets."

The Gospel has a similar scene. John tells Jesus that the disciples saw someone driving out demons in Jesus' name and tried to stop him "because he doesn't follow us." Jesus answers, "Don't forbid him... For whoever is not against us is on our side." Even a cup of water given in Christ's name will be rewarded. God's Spirit is not limited to our group.

Then Jesus turns very serious. Anyone who causes "one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble" would be better thrown into the sea. He uses strong images: if your hand, your foot, or your eye causes you to sin, cut it off. He does not mean this literally, but he means it seriously: sin must be removed from our lives at any cost, because eternal life is at stake.

Saint James speaks to the rich in burning words. Riches gained by injustice will rot, and "the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you have kept back by fraud, cry out." God hears the cry of the exploited.

This week, rejoice in the good done by people outside your own circle, and thank God for it. Ask yourself honestly what in your life leads you, or others, into sin, and take one decisive step to cut it out.
